observedSigns: Symptoms starting from the bottom and moving upward
possibleCauses: Fungal infection favored by high humidity
followUpQuestions: Are there any concentric rings (like a target pattern) visible inside the dark brown spots?
Are the spots appearing on the stems or fruit as well, or just the leaves?
How close together are your tomato plants planted?
Have you noticed any small black dots in the center of the spots?
immediateActions: Remove and destroy the most severely affected lower leaves to improve airflow.
Avoid overhead watering; water only at the base of the plant to keep leaves dry.
Ensure there is adequate spacing between plants to allow for better air circulation.
Clean your tools thoroughly after touching affected plants to prevent spreading the issue.
assessment.whenToSeekHelp: If the spots continue to spread rapidly to the upper leaves and fruit despite removing affected foliage, or if more than 30% of the plant is affected, please consult your local agricultural extension worker for a professional assessment.

uncertainty.reason: The symptoms described are consistent with common fungal blights, but a definitive diagnosis cannot be made without visual confirmation of the lesion patterns and the absence of other potential nutrient or pest issues.
